name: Accra
subtitle: Accra, capital of Ghana: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,782,150 people lived in the historic Accra urban agglomeration in the 2021 census (over 5.4 million in Greater Accra Region).
Capital of Ghana since 1877 when it succeeded Cape Coast, it developed from historic Ga coastal fishing and trading settlements.
Black Star Square and Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park stand as global monuments to Pan-African emancipation and modern democracy.

parts.text: Accra originated as an ancestral homeland of the Ga people, who developed coastal fishing and trading communities in Jamestown and Usshertown surrounding 17th-century European fortified posts.
In 1877, British colonial authorities transferred the capital of the Gold Coast from Cape Coast to Accra, spurring its rapid growth as an administrative and railway terminus.
Following national independence in March 1957 under Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, Accra became a vibrant continental capital of Pan-African solidarity, intellectual renaissance, and creative arts.

blocks.prompt: About how many people lived in the historic Accra urban agglomeration in the 2021 census?

parts.text: 1,782,150 across the historic urban core in the 2021 PHC census by Ghana Statistical Service, while Greater Accra Region as a whole recorded 5,455,692 residents.

items.text: British Fort James is established along the Ga coast.
Accra becomes the colonial capital of the British Gold Coast, succeeding Cape Coast.
Ghana achieves independence under Kwame Nkrumah; Accra becomes capital of sovereign Ghana.
Black Star Gate and Independence Square are dedicated.
The national census counts over 5.4 million inhabitants in Greater Accra Region.
